items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: Bob Foster, Red Island, Otis Johnson, Agen Bollett, we had one trombone at the time.

ctx.x: One time, we were at the Saratoga Club, and we were working the whole year round, not even one night off in the whole year. So we told Russell, we said, man, we're tired. We're going to leave there. We're going to the Roseland Ballroom two months back to Saratoga. Tour, make theater, Lowest State and all those places, go to Washington, D.C., come back. So finally we took two weeks off. Russell put another band in the Saratoga, and said, well, these fellas have two weeks. And Jelly was there that night. He heard…
The man said, oh, Jelly, come on, come on.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: So Nick was in the band then.

ctx.x: This Paul? Yeah. So the chair came up and moved, so this chick jumped up and peed all over himself and run down. Now, but the whole band, Louie and all of us in one room, man, they're the liberty rooms. And that's the way to catch you, that's the way you got to be sleeping, man. One guy stands beside the wall. About six guys crossed the bed, a little bit of bed, sleeping, sitting on the floor. I mean, I'll cut a sandwich's throat. I'm a man. I ain't scared of a sandwich in here. Come out and fight like a man.…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: Is Nicholas in that group? I didn't recognize you. Albert, yeah. Albert's in that group.

ctx.x: very well. Yeah. And here's another picture of Louis Russell. You see this Louis Russell
here. Oh, yes. I think I've seen that picture. Let's see. Is Nicholas in that group? I didn't recognize you. Albert, yeah. Albert's in that group. Oh, yeah.
A picture of Ralph Sutton. Yeah, that's me and Ralph, man. Both of us was juiced
